messages:
Erica (AM): kicking off POC with Acme — they want VPC peering + mTLS. hitting TLS handshake failures to our private endpoint, can netsec help?
Chris (NetEng): @Erica can you paste the curl error + dst ip?
Erica (AM): curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.10.2.5:443
Erica (AM): logs:
```[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] connect to 10.10.2.5:443 TLS handshake failed: alert certificate_unknown
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] client hello SNI: acc.example.internal
```
Mina (Sales-Eng): do they have split-horizon DNS? SNI not matching cert is common with private zones.
Devon (SRE): also check whether their egress NAT is rewriting IPs — our allowed source list expects their peering subnet. If NATted, cert validation still uses hostnames though.
Erica (AM): customer says private DNS resolves acc.redwood.local -> 10.10.2.5 and they use that name for tests. cert CN shows model.redwood.example (public).
Chris (NetEng): ok that explains it — hostname in cert != hostname client used. SNI in ClientHello will be the internal name, cert won't match.
Mina (Sales-Eng): options: 1) they map the public hostname (model.redwood.example) in their private zone to 10.10.2.5, so SNI matches cert; 2) upload a private cert that includes their internal name (requires enterprise plan / custom cert support); 3) TLS termination/proxy in their VPC with SANs.
Sarah (Security): we prefer customers keep the public hostname but map privately. Uploading certs has compliance implications — need contract + cert chain validation.
Erica (AM): customer reluctant to change split-horizon. asked if mTLS auth would bypass SNI mismatch.
Devon (SRE): mTLS authenticates client, but it doesn't change hostname validation. SNI is still used for routing and cert selection. mTLS won't fix hostname mismatch.
Chris (NetEng): quick diag commands for them:
```bash
# verify SNI in client hello (openssl s_client)
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.2.5:443 -servername model.redwood.example
```
and check cert subject with `-showcerts`.
Erica (AM): they ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.2.5:443 -servername acc.redwood.local` and cert subject was CN=model.redwood.example -> mismatch.
Mina (Sales-Eng): I'll capture pricing note: custom cert upload and private endpoint cert support is available on Dedicated/Private. need to confirm in quote whether Acme is qualifying for that.
Devon (SRE): also saw intermittent 429s when they replay tests — that's our rate limiting kicking in on bursts. For POC we can temporarily raise their quota.
deploybot: infra ticket created: #7412 — request to increase rate limit to 200r/s for acct acme-poc (created by Devon).
Devon (SRE): I asked infra to add allow rule for their NAT range 10.10.0.0/16 to expected source list. once added will retest.
Erica (AM): after customer added a CNAME in their private zone pointing model.redwood.example -> 10.10.2.5 and we allowed their NAT range, tls handshake succeeded and responses are flowing :thumbsup:
Mina (Sales-Eng): filing next steps: 1) follow up on custom cert entitlement + pricing, 2) document DNS mapping best-practices in deal repo, 3) confirm rate-limit permanently for Dedicated plan.
Sarah (Security): add to SQA checklist: private DNS mapping to public host, cert SAN validation, NAT source allowance, and documented audit trail for any uploaded certs.
Erica (AM): customer happy, moving to technical acceptance. will open new thread if anything regresses. thanks team!
